tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. # Glossary

Use these names in code, UI, PRs and issues. Avoid synonyms such as "edit", "proposal" or "patch" for a Suggestion.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Document** | The Markdown text in the editor. The only thing the app persists (`localStorage`). |
| **Block** | A top-level node of the CodeMirror Markdown syntax tree: paragraph, heading, list, blockquote, code block. A whole list is one Block. |
| **Target** | The range an AI request is about: the selection, or the Block under the cursor when nothing is selected. |
| **Neighbors** | The 2 Blocks before and the 2 after the Target, plus the document title (first `#`) and the current section heading. Sent as context. |
| **Instruction** | What the user asks for: a Quick action or free text. |
| **Quick action** | A preset Instruction: Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar. |
| **Suggestion** | A proposed replacement for a range of the Document. It lives outside the Document (an overlay) until accepted. Holds: range, original text, Replacement, Rationale, refine history. |
| **Replacement** | The new text the AI proposes for a Suggestion's range. |
| **Rationale** | One short sentence from the AI explaining the change, in the Document's language. Shown on hover, or when the cursor is inside the Suggestion. |
| **Active Suggestion** | The most recently created Suggestion, or the one containing the cursor. The only one that shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. |
| **Accept** | Apply the Replacement to the Document. A normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. |
| **Reject** | Drop the Suggestion. Not undoable in v1. |
| **Refine** | A follow-up Instruction on an open Suggestion. Produces a new Replacement in place. The diff is always against the original text. |
| **Discard** | Remove a Suggestion because the user edited inside its range or a newer Suggestion overlapped it. Shows a discreet notice. |
| **Review pass** | On-demand request: the AI reads the whole Document (Blocks numbered `p1`, `p2`, …) and returns up to 6 Suggestions, one per Block, streamed one by one. |
| **Focus** | Optional free text that narrows a Review pass ("focus on tone"). |
| **Draft** | (Backlog) Streamed, not-yet-validated Replacement text shown without a diff. |
| **Bake-off** | Scripted comparison of candidate models on the same requests ([ADR 0010](docs/chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)). |
| **AI call record** | Per-call log entry for verification: task, model, provider, tokens, cost, timings, finish reason, generation id. |
| **Gate** | A point where the orchestrator stops for the maintainer's decision. |

## What to build

**Type:** AFK

A **Review** button in the toolbar opens an optional Focus field. The app sends the whole Document with numbered Blocks. Without a Focus, the AI looks at clarity, concision, grammar and tone consistency.

The model returns at most 6 edits, streamed through `Output.array` + `elementStream`, most important first. Each validated element becomes a Suggestion on its Block as soon as it arrives, with the adaptive diff and a Rationale. Code blocks and Blocks that already have an open Suggestion are skipped. While review Suggestions are open, Accept all and Reject all are available, and each Suggestion can still be resolved on its own.

Decisions: [0002](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0002-structured-output-app-owned-anchors.md), [0004](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0004-user-triggered-ai-and-review-pass.md), [0007](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md), [0008](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/blob/main/docs/chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TDD covers mapping edits to Suggestions: an unknown `blockId` is dropped, an unchanged Replacement is dropped, occupied Blocks and code blocks are skipped, and there are at most 6.
- [ ] On the sample Document, the first Suggestion appears before the stream ends, and the time to the first Suggestion is recorded.
- [ ] A Focus visibly changes the kind of Suggestions returned.
- [ ] Accept all and Reject all work, and single Accept / Reject / Refine still work on review Suggestions.
- [ ] AI call records and screenshots are in `docs/chiri/verification/`, and `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md` is updated.

# 0002. Structured model output; the app owns the anchors

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q10, Q39

## Context

What can go wrong with a model's answer here:

| Failure | Plain text | Structured JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Wrapper chatter ("Sure! Here's…", code fences) | happens, needs cleaning | gone, the schema enforces the shape |
| Changes beyond the Instruction | happens | happens equally |
| Invented content | happens | happens equally |
| Wrong location (quotes text that doesn't exist) | impossible, the app knows the range | **new risk**, if the model picks the location |

The diff itself guards against rows 2 and 3: every change is visible before Accept. Structure removes row 1 and makes the answer checkable, but can create row 4.

## Decision

- **Strict structured outputs:** `structured_outputs` with OpenRouter `provider.require_parameters: true`, so only providers that support it are used. One zod schema per shape is both the validator and the source of the JSON Schema.
- **Target requests and Refine:** the app already knows the range. The model returns `{ replacement, rationale }`.
- **Review pass:** the app numbers Blocks (`p1`, `p2`, …) before sending. The model returns `{ edits: [{ blockId, replacement, rationale }] }` and never copies text to say where. A Block is a top-level node of the Markdown syntax tree; a whole list is one Block.
- **Wire shape with AI SDK `Output.array`:** the SDK owns the wrapper, so the Review pass wire shape is `{ elements: [...] }`; each element is `{ blockId, replacement, rationale }`.
- **App-side validation:** drop an item when `replacement` equals the original or `blockId` is unknown. On invalid output, retry once silently, then show an error card.

## Consequences

- No chatter, a Rationale for every change, and answers the app can check.
- Review pass granularity is one Block: two changes in one paragraph become one Suggestion, and a long list is a single Suggestion.

# Implementation plan

Runbook for the implementation orchestrator. The planning session produced this plan, the [ADRs](chiri/adr/) and the issues below. Read [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) and [GLOSSARY.md](../GLOSSARY.md) first.

## Roles

| Role | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `opus` | Runs the loop below, owns gates, merges PRs. Claude Code only, so every session log lands in `~/.claude/projects/`. |
| Implementer | `sonnet` subagent | One at a time, in the orchestrator's checkout, on the slice branch. |
| Reviewer, first pass | `opus` subagent, effort `medium` | Two axes, as in the `code-review` skill: **Standards** (against [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)) and **Spec** (against the issue and its ADRs). |
| Reviewer, later passes | `sonnet` subagent | Re-checks the fixes until no real findings remain. |

Slices run **sequentially**. Each builds on the previous one, and running them in parallel would collide on `package.json` and shared modules.

## Loop per slice

1. Branch from up-to-date `main`, using the name in the table below.
2. Implementer: TDD the pure modules the issue lists, then the UI.
3. Run the definition of done ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#definition-of-done-every-slice)): tests, Biome, build.
4. Verify the acceptance criteria in a real browser with `agent-browser`. Record the AI calls and screenshots ([AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#ai-call-records)) and update [chiri/ai-costs.md](chiri/ai-costs.md).
5. Open the PR with the `pr` skill and the [template](../.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md).
6. First review (`opus`, medium), fix, then re-review (`sonnet`) until clean. Note the review outcome in the PR.
7. Squash merge.
8. If the slice ends at a gate, stop and wait.

## Slices

| # | Issue | Branch | Scope | Depends on | Gate after | Est. |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [#1](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/1) | `feat/editor-shell` | Vite + React + TS + Tailwind, CodeMirror with styled Markdown, sample Document, `localStorage`, proxy, missing-key banner, Biome, Vitest | — | — | 45 min |
| 2 | [#2](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/2) | `feat/model-client-bakeoff` | AI SDK client, zod schemas, prompt building, Block extraction, AI call records, `scripts/bakeoff.ts`, `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md` | 1 | **A** | 60 min |
| 3 | [#3](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/3) | `feat/selection-suggestions` | Selection bubble, `Cmd+K`, Quick actions, Suggestion state and mapping, adaptive diff, overlay decorations, Accept / Reject, Rationale, errors | 2, Gate A | **B** | 90 min |
| 4 | [#4](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/4) | `feat/refine` | Refine on the Active Suggestion, history, diff against original | 3, Gate B | — | 30 min |
| 5 | [#5](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/5) | `feat/review-pass` | Review pass with Focus, numbered Blocks, streamed validated Suggestions (max 6), skip occupied Blocks, Accept all / Reject all | 4 | — | 45 min |
| 6 | [#6](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/6) | `docs/readme-and-sessions` | Final README, backlog review, session export script, `ai-sessions/` | 5 | **C** | 30 min |

That is about 5 h 15 of work, plus 30–40 min of reviews. If time runs short, shrink slice 5 first.

## Gates

- **A, after slice 2 (model):** present `docs/chiri/bakeoff.md`, with outputs side by side, latency, cost and validity. The maintainer picks the model or models. Update [ADR 0010](chiri/adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md) to Accepted and set the default in `.env.example`. If any Target-request latency is above ~3 s, flag the Draft reopen rule ([ADR 0008](chiri/adr/0008-validated-streaming-only.md)).
- **B, after slice 3 (core flow):** the maintainer tries select → Suggestion → Accept / Reject in the browser. Fix taste issues before Refine and the Review pass build on top.
- **C, before merging slice 6 (submission):** final look at the README, cost log, sessions and repo.

## Budget

US$5 OpenRouter cap. The Bake-off should stay under US$0.50. Every model call made during verification goes into [chiri/ai-costs.md](chiri/ai-costs.md). If the running total passes US$2, stop and tell the maintainer.

## Session logs (slice 6)

The challenge requires raw, unedited session files committed to the repo. Only secrets may be masked.

- Source: every folder in `~/.claude/projects/` whose name starts with `-home-walter-Github-chiri-ai-editor` (this covers every worktree). Copy each session's `<id>.jsonl` and its sibling `<id>/` folder (subagents, tool results) as they are. Skip non-session files such as `memory/`.
- Destination: `ai-sessions/<project-folder>/…`.
- Masking: replace OpenRouter keys (`sk-or-…`) with `sk-or-***MASKED***`, and nothing else.
- The script lives in `scripts/` and runs last, after the final PR text is written, so it captures as much as possible. Note in the README that the orchestrator session continues after the export.
- Claude Code deletes transcripts older than `cleanupPeriodDays`, 30 days by default. Export before then.

# 0004. User-triggered AI, plus an on-demand Review pass

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q5, Q12, Q28

## Context

"The user is always in control", but the AI should feel like a co-author, not something that completes the whole Document.

## Decision

- **The AI acts only when asked.**
- **Selection bubble:** Quick actions (Shorter, Clearer, More formal, Fix grammar) plus a free-text "Ask AI…" field. `Cmd/Ctrl+K` opens the same field. With no selection, the Target is the Block under the cursor.
- **Review pass:** a toolbar button with an optional Focus. Without Focus, the AI looks at clarity, concision, grammar and tone consistency. It returns at most 6 Suggestions, most important first. It skips code blocks and Blocks that already have an open Suggestion.
- **No slash commands, no proactive hints.**
- Many Suggestions can be open at once from day one.

## Consequences

- Predictable, cheap, and the user is in control.
- The Review pass gives the "colleague marking up my draft" feeling without ambient noise.
- The 6-Suggestion cap leaves issues untouched in long, rough Documents. A wall of red and green would read as "the AI rewrote everything".

## Alternatives considered

- **Proactive hints on idle:** the strongest co-author feel, but it burns tokens under a US$5 cap, is noisy, and is hard to tune.
- **Slash commands:** they pull toward "generate at cursor", which is close to completing the Document.
- **Free-text only, no Quick actions:** less discoverable. Reviewers would have to invent what to ask.
# 0007. Suggestion lifecycle

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q13, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q25, Q32

## Context

Suggestions are overlays ([0001](0001-inline-overlay-suggestions.md)) and the user keeps typing while they are open or in flight.

## Decision

- **Edits outside a Suggestion:** its range is mapped through the change (CodeMirror `ChangeSet` mapping).
- **Edits inside an open Suggestion, or inside an in-flight request's Target:** Discard it, with a discreet notice ("Suggestion discarded: the text changed").
- **Overlaps:** a new request over an open Suggestion replaces it, so the last one wins. The Review pass skips Blocks with open Suggestions.
- **Active Suggestion:** shows the Accept / Reject / Refine toolbar. Its Rationale shows on hover, and when the text cursor is inside it (keyboard users can't hover). Other Suggestions show only the inline diff.
- **Keys, with the cursor inside a Suggestion:** `Cmd/Ctrl+Enter` Accepts, `Esc` Rejects. Accept is a normal edit, so `Cmd+Z` undoes it. Reject is not undoable in v1. A Review pass also offers Accept all and Reject all.
- **Refine:** a follow-up Instruction on the Active Suggestion. The new Replacement replaces the old one in place. The diff is always against the original text. History stays in memory, with no version arrows in v1.
- **Persistence:** only the Document text goes to `localStorage`. Open Suggestions are lost on reload.
- **Failures:**
  - Missing key: banner ([0005](0005-local-only-vite-proxy.md)).
  - Failed call (network, `402` out of credit, `429`): the Suggestion becomes an error card with Retry. `402` gets its own message.
  - Invalid output: one silent retry, then the error card.
  - Timeout: 30 s.

## Consequences

- Simple, honest rules. A user who bumps into a Suggestion loses it, and can ask again.
- An accidental `Esc` loses a Suggestion. An undoable Reject is in the backlog.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep a stale Suggestion with "regenerate":** an extra state, and an old diff can't be drawn over changed text.
- **Lock the range while a Suggestion is open:** takes control away from the user.
- **Block new requests until the old Suggestion is resolved:** friction.
- **Allow overlapping Suggestions:** accepting one breaks the other.
- **Rationale always visible, or in a side panel:** the side panel drifts toward the chatbot sidebar.
# 0008. Stream only where each piece arrives validated

- Status: Accepted (2026-10-28)
- Source: planning session, Q24, Q31

## Context

Streaming has three costs here: parsing half-finished JSON, a diff that jitters while text arrives (not-yet-rewritten original text shows as deleted), and showing text before it is validated.

AI SDK v7, verified in its docs on 2026-10-28:
- With `Output.object`, `partialOutputStream` yields partial objects that "cannot be validated against your provided schema". Only the final output is validated.
- With `Output.array`, `elementStream` yields each element "complete and validated against your element schema".

## Decision

- **Review pass:** stream with `Output.array` and `elementStream`. Each Suggestion appears once it is schema-validated by the SDK and checked by the app (`blockId` exists, Replacement differs from the original).
- **Target requests and Refine:** not streamed. `Output.object`, validated before anything is shown.
- **Reopen rule:** if the chosen model's median latency for Target requests is above ~3 s, add a Draft preview: streamed text without a diff that turns into the diff once validated.

## Consequences

- The slowest call, the Review pass, shows its first Suggestion early, with no validation trade-off.
- Target requests stay simple: one state, validated before display.
- The Draft preview sits in the backlog behind a measurable rule.

## Alternatives considered

- **No streaming at all:** simplest, but the Review pass waits for all 6 Suggestions.
- **Stream everything, including a Draft for Target requests:** matches the challenge's "live preview" idea, but adds a visual state and a Draft that can fail validation and vanish.

33:## Notes for the choice
34-
35-Written by hand after the run. The tables above and below are generated.
36-
37-- **Timeout.** The runs used 60 s for the Review pass. After the run it was set back to 30 s, as [ADR 0007](adr/0007-suggestion-lifecycle.md) says; every model except `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` finished its Review pass in under 8 s.
38-- **Validity.** All 9 models returned schema-valid output on the first try in every request: 0 retries and 0 edits dropped by the app checks, in all three runs. The strict JSON schema with `require_parameters: true` held for every candidate.
39-- **Latency.** Six models have a median Target request under ~3 s in all three runs (see the table below). `google/gemini-3.8-flash` (3.8 to 5.4 s), `google/gemini-4-argon` (5.0 to 10.3 s) and `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` (11 to 15 s) are over the ADR 0008 line, so picking one of them reopens the Draft preview.
40-- **Review pass.** The first Suggestion arrives after 30 to 85 % of the total time in this run: `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` is the earliest (1.6 s of 5.5 s), `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` the latest (4.2 s of 5.1 s). `qwen/qwen3.8-flash` finished the Review pass once in three runs (26.9 s) and timed out at 60 s the other two times.
41-- **Rationale language.** The Document is English. `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` write the Rationale in German, French, Dutch, Italian, Portuguese and others, in 7 of 9 and 2 of 9 Rationales in this run. They did it in the earlier runs too, with different wording of rule 5. With the final wording the other seven models never did; the two small Gemini models slipped only in run 1. This is a rule 5 failure, and it is the main quality difference between the cheap models.
42-- **What the models edit.** Most Review passes pick the same Blocks: p3 (the overlong paragraph), p5 (the slang), p8 (the list), p9 (the repeated review rule) and p12 (the typo). `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` skips p9 and `google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` skips p3.
43-- **Cost.** US$0.0559 for this run. For the same 5 requests `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` costs roughly 20 to 27 times what `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` and `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` cost, and `google/gemini-4-argon` roughly 15 to 19 times.

**Running total:** US$0.252 of 5.00

Notes on slice 2:
- The first nine rows are the final Bake-off run, the one in [bakeoff.md](bakeoff.md): US$0.0559, well under the US$0.50 budget. The other rows are what it took to get the prompts right (two full runs, prompt checks, dry runs), so the slice total is about US$0.23.
- Latency for the Bake-off rows is the median Target request / the Review pass, client wall time. A dash means the request failed (Qwen's Review pass timed out at 60 s).
- Cost per call is the `usage.cost` OpenRouter returns. Calls that time out return no usage, so their cost is estimated from the rise of the key's `usage` counter (US$8.743 to US$8.973 across the slice, minus the recorded rows). That counter is the lifetime usage of the key, not this project's.
- OpenRouter publishes `/generation` data (provider, `latency`, `generation_time`) about a minute after the call, so the client records a call right away and enriches it later.

Notes on slice 3:
- Slice cost is about US$0.011: 11 recorded calls US$0.0085, three calls without a record about US$0.0022, and the aborted request, whose usage OpenRouter did not report. The key's usage counter rose by about US$0.0104 over the slice, which agrees with the sum within the error of its starting point. The slice budget was US$0.10.
- The forced-failure checks never reached OpenRouter, so they cost nothing.

Notes on slice 4:
- Slice cost is about US$0.0071: 8 real calls, all recorded (5 Quick actions to open Suggestions, 3 Refines). The failures, the aborted requests and the stub never reached OpenRouter. The slice budget was US$0.05.
- A Refine request carries about 100 input tokens more than a Quick action (history and latest Replacement), so it costs about US$0.001 against US$0.0009.

# Slice 4 verification: Refine

Issue [#4](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/4). Checked on 2026-10-28 in a real browser (`agent-browser`, headless Chrome, 1200 x 900) against `pnpm dev`, with `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` ([ADR 0010](../adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)) through the Vite proxy, on the sample Document.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| TDD covers the Refine prompt (original text, Instruction history, latest Replacement) and the Suggestion history update | Pass | `src/ai/prompts.test.ts` (`buildRefinePrompt`: original, history in order and numbered, latest Replacement, new Instruction, Neighbors, title and section, enclosing Block, the 5 fixed rules), `src/suggestions/state.test.ts` (69: begin, resolve, unchanged, failure, retry, Accept / Reject / Discard / mapping while refining), `src/suggestions/instruction.test.ts`, `src/editor/suggestion-runtime.test.ts` (25), `src/editor/refine-input.test.ts` (8), `src/editor/suggestion-keymap.test.ts` (10), `src/editor/suggestion-field.test.ts` (14). `pnpm test`: 426 tests green |
| The Active Suggestion's toolbar has Refine, which opens a small input | Pass | [4-1](img/4-1.png) (third button), [4-2](img/4-2.png) (input focused inside the toolbar card). `Esc` in the input closes only the input, the Suggestion stays. `Ctrl+K` with the cursor inside a ready Suggestion opens the input, not the Ask bubble |
| Two consecutive Refines each update the Suggestion in place, and the diff stays against the original text | Pass | "make it shorter" then "now more formal" on p3: [4-3](img/4-3.png) (working), [4-4](img/4-4.png) (first Refine), [4-5](img/4-5.png) (second). Same Suggestion, same range, still Active, new Rationale each time. The struck text is the original paragraph in every frame, and the Document string was unchanged |
| The model gets the original, the Neighbors, every previous Instruction and the latest Replacement | Pass | The body of the third Refine (read from the wrapped `fetch`): `<original>` is the untouched paragraph, `<context-before>` and `<context-after>` hold the Neighbors, "Previous instructions, oldest first" lists the Shorter Quick action text, "make it shorter" and "now more formal", `<latest-replacement>` is the output of the second Refine, then "New instruction: drop the adjectives". Task labels read `refine p3 → now more formal` |
| While refining, the Replacement stays visible and shows that it is working | Pass | [4-3](img/4-3.png) and [4-10](img/4-10.png): the Replacement keeps showing, a slow shimmer runs over the inserted text, and the toolbar button reads "Refining…" (disabled, `aria-busy`). Word-level diffs shimmer on each inserted word. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the CSS falls back to a static tint (not exercised in the browser) |
| Accept after Refine applies the latest Replacement, `Ctrl+Z` restores the original | Pass | After two Refines and a third, `Ctrl+Enter`: the paragraph is the latest Replacement, no Suggestion left, [4-9](img/4-9.png). `Ctrl+Z` gave back the exact original Document string |
| Accept and Reject still work during a Refine and abort it | Pass | Cancel (`Esc`) during a Refine: the first `Esc` cancels the Refine and aborts the request (`aborted` in the record), the Suggestion keeps its Replacement; the second `Esc` Rejects it, no notice, Document unchanged. The same two-step `Esc` dismisses the error of a failed Refine (see the review re-check below). Accept (`Ctrl+Enter`) during a Refine: the current Replacement is applied, [4-12](img/4-12.png), request aborted, `Ctrl+Z` restores the original |
| Typing inside the Suggestion during a Refine Discards it with the notice and aborts the request | Pass | [4-10](img/4-10.png) then [4-11](img/4-11.png): one key inside the range, toast "Suggestion discarded: the text changed", the in-flight request's `AbortSignal` was aborted, the record says `aborted` |
| A failed Refine shows Retry without losing the current Replacement | Pass | Network failure: [4-6](img/4-6.png). The error sits inside the toolbar card, the struck original, the Replacement and the Rationale are unchanged, Accept / Reject / Refine are still there. Retry failing again with a 402 body gives the own message, [4-7](img/4-7.png). Retry again with the real model: the Suggestion updates in place, [4-8](img/4-8.png), and the request body lists the earlier Instructions without the two failed attempts |
| "No change suggested" when a Refine returns the current Replacement | Pass | A stubbed answer equal to the Replacement: toast "No change suggested", Replacement and Rationale kept, the Suggestion is idle again, [4-13](img/4-13.png) |
| The input survives a toolbar re-render | Pass | Typing "abc" in the Refine input, then hovering the Suggestion and leaving it (which re-renders the card): text and focus kept, [4-14](img/4-14.png) |
| AI call records and screenshots are here, `ai-costs.md` is updated | Pass | This file and [ai-costs.md](../ai-costs.md) |

| [4-15](img/4-15.png) | Review re-check: a failed Refine on a non-Active Suggestion (dotted underline) with its error in the hover card |
| [4-16](img/4-16.png) | Review re-check: Refine in flight on a deletion-only diff, shimmer on the struck words |

## How the checks were driven

- Real key presses and clicks: `Ctrl+K` (Ask bubble and Refine input), `Enter`, `Esc`, `Ctrl+Enter`, `Ctrl+Z`, typed characters, clicks on the toolbar buttons. Selections and the cursor were set with `view.dispatch`, reaching the view through `.cm-content`'s `cmTile.view`.
- Forced failures wrapped `window.fetch` from `eval`: a `TypeError` for the network failure, a 402 body for out of credit. A fetch that never answers (and honors the abort signal) held a Refine in flight for the Accept, Reject and Discard checks and for the shimmer frames. A canned answer stood in for the model on the "no change" check. None of these reached OpenRouter, so they cost nothing.
- The log was dumped from `window.__aiCalls` after about 70 s, so the generation endpoint had filled in provider and OpenRouter latency.

## AI call records

Read from `window.__aiCalls` (`agent-browser eval`) and formatted with `formatRecordsTable` from `src/ai/records.ts`. Rows with no model served are the two forced failures, the three aborted requests (never answered, no usage reported) and the stub (`stub`, cost 0).

# agent-browser core

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no
Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact
`@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of
parsing raw HTML.

Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are
covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser
web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).

## The core loop

```bash

agent-browser wait @e1                     # until an element appears
agent-browser wait 2000                    # dumb wait, milliseconds (last resort)
agent-browser wait --text "Success"        # until the text appears on the page
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"    # until URL matches pattern (glob)
```

After any page-changing action, pick one:

- Wait for a specific element you expect to appear: `wait @ref` or `wait --text "..."`.
- Wait for URL change: `wait --url "**/new-page"`.

Avoid bare `wait 2000` except when debugging — it makes scripts slow and

## Common workflows

### Log in

```bash
agent-browser open https://app.example.com/login
agent-browser snapshot -i

# Pick the email/password refs out of the snapshot, then:
agent-browser fill @e3 "user@example.com"
agent-browser fill @e4 "hunter2"
agent-browser click @e5
agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"
agent-browser snapshot -i
```

Credentials in shell history are a leak. For anything sensitive, use the
auth vault (see [references/authentication.md](references/authentication.md)):

```bash
agent-browser auth save my-app --url https://app.example.com/login \
  --username user@example.com --password-stdin
# (type password, Ctrl+D)

agent-browser auth login my-app    # fills + clicks, waits for form
```

### Persist session across runs

```bash
# Log in once, save cookies + localStorage
agent-browser state save ./auth.json

# Later runs start already-logged-in
agent-browser --state ./auth.json open https://app.example.com
```

Or use `--session-name` for auto-save/restore:

```bash
AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION_NAME=my-app agent-browser open https://app.example.com
# State is auto-saved and restored on subsequent runs with the same name.
```

### Extract data

```bash
# Structured snapshot (best for AI reasoning over page content)
agent-browser snapshot -i --json > page.json

# Targeted extraction with refs
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser get text @e5
agent-browser get attr @e10 href

# Arbitrary shape via JavaScript
cat <<'EOF' | agent-browser eval --stdin
const rows = document.querySelectorAll("table tbody tr");
Array.from(rows).map(r => ({
  name: r.cells[0].innerText,
  price: r.cells[1].innerText,
}));
EOF
```

Prefer `eval --stdin` (heredoc) or `eval -b <base64>` for any JS with
quotes or special characters. Inline `agent-browser eval "..."` works
only for simple expressions.

### Screenshot

```bash
agent-browser screenshot                        # temp path, printed on stdout
agent-browser screenshot page.png               # specific path
agent-browser screenshot --full full.png        # full scroll height
agent-browser screenshot --annotate map.png     # numbered labels + legend keyed to snapshot refs
```

`--annotate` is designed for multimodal models: each label `[N]` maps to ref `@eN`.

### Handle multiple pages via tabs

```bash
agent-browser tab                      # list open tabs (with stable tabId)
agent-browser tab new https://docs...  # open a new tab (and switch to it)
agent-browser tab 2                    # switch to tab 2
agent-browser tab close 2              # close tab 2
```

Stable `tabId`s mean `tab 2` points at the same tab across commands even
when other tabs open or close. After switching, refs from a prior snapshot
on a different tab no longer apply — re-snapshot.

### Run multiple browsers in parallel

Each `--session <name>` is an isolated browser with its own cookies, tabs,
and refs. Useful for testing multi-user flows or parallel scraping:

```bash
agent-browser --session a open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session b open https://app.example.com
agent-browser --session a fill @e1 "alice@test.com"
agent-browser --session b fill @e1 "bob@test.com"
```

`AGENT_BROWSER_SESSION=myapp` sets the default session for the current
shell.

### Mock network requests

```bash
agent-browser network route "**/api/users" --body '{"users":[]}'   # stub a response
agent-browser network route "**/analytics" --abort                 # block entirely
agent-browser network requests                                     # inspect what fired
agent-browser network har start                                    # record all traffic
# ... perform actions ...
agent-browser network har stop /tmp/trace.har
```

### Record a video of the workflow

```bash
agent-browser record start demo.webm
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser click @e3
agent-browser record stop
```

See [references/video-recording.md](references/video-recording.md) for
codec options, GIF export, and more.

### Iframes

Iframes are auto-inlined in the snapshot — their refs work transparently:

```bash
agent-browser snapshot -i
# @e3 [Iframe] "payment-frame"
#   @e4 [input] "Card number"
#   @e5 [button] "Pay"

agent-browser fill @e4 "4111111111111111"
agent-browser click @e5
```

To scope a snapshot to an iframe (for focus or deep nesting):

```bash
agent-browser frame @e3      # switch context to the iframe
agent-browser snapshot -i
agent-browser frame main     # back to main frame
```

### Dialogs

`alert` and `beforeunload` are auto-accepted so agents never block. For
`confirm` and `prompt`:

```bash
agent-browser dialog status          # is there a pending dialog?
agent-browser dialog accept           # accept
agent-browser dialog accept "text"    # accept with prompt input
agent-browser dialog dismiss          # cancel
```

## Diagnosing install issues

If a command fails unexpectedly (`Unknown command`, `Failed to connect`,
stale daemons, version mismatches after `upgrade`, missing Chrome, etc.)
run `doctor` before anything else:

```bash
agent-browser doctor                     # full diagnosis (env, Chrome, daemons, config, providers, network, launch test)
agent-browser doctor --offline --quick   # fast, local-only
agent-browser doctor --fix               # also run destructive repairs (reinstall Chrome, purge old state, ...)
agent-browser doctor --json              # structured output for programmatic consumption
```

`doctor` auto-cleans stale socket/pid/version sidecar files on every run.
Destructive actions require `--fix`. Exit code is `0` if all checks pass
(warnings OK), `1` if any fail.

## Troubleshooting

**"Ref not found" / "Element not found: @eN"**
Page changed since the snapshot. Run `agent-browser snapshot -i` again,
then use the new refs.

**Element exists in the DOM but not in the snapshot**
It's probably off-screen or not yet rendered. Try:

```bash
agent-browser scroll down 1000
agent-browser snapshot -i
# or
agent-browser wait --text "..."
agent-browser snapshot -i
```

**Click does nothing / overlay swallows the click**
Some modals and cookie banners block other clicks. Snapshot, find the
dismiss/close button, click it, then re-snapshot.

**Fill / type doesn't work**
Some custom input components intercept key events. Try:

```bash
agent-browser focus @e1
agent-browser keyboard inserttext "text"    # bypasses key events
# or
agent-browser keyboard type "text"          # raw keystrokes, no selector
```

**Page needs JS you can't get right in one shot**
Use `eval --stdin` with a heredoc instead of inline:

```bash
cat <<'EOF' | agent-browser eval --stdin
// Complex script with quotes, backticks, whatever
document.querySelectorAll('[data-id]').length
EOF
```

**Cross-origin iframe not accessible**
Cross-origin iframes that block accessibility tree access are silently
skipped. Use `frame "#iframe"` to switch into them explicitly if the
parent opts in, otherwise the iframe's contents aren't available via
snapshot — fall back to `eval` in the iframe's origin or use the
`--headers` flag to satisfy CORS.

## Why we are changing


For the past two years our team has frozen all production deployments on Fridays, a rule introduced after a painful weekend incident in 2022 that was entirely reasonable at the time but has since hardened into a habit nobody questions, even though it slows down every sprint, pushes risky changes into the early part of the week when the team is already stretched thin by planning and support duties, and makes it harder to ship the small fixes that customers are actually waiting for.


Our pipeline has changed a lot since then. Every deploy now runs automated smoke tests, rolls out to ten percent of traffic first, and reverts itself if the error rate rises. The Friday freeze no longer protects us from much.


Honestly, the old freeze was a total pain and everyone kinda hated it. So we're ditching it, no big deal, but please don't be that person who pushes a huge change at 5pm on Friday and then vanishes for the weekend lol.


## What changes


Starting on the first of next month, you may deploy on any weekday, as long as the following conditions are met:


- Tests are passing on the main branch
- Get a review from a second engineer
- Rollback plan, you must write one in the pull request.
- No deploys during the on-call handover

readonly generationId: string | null
  readonly error: string | null
}

export type ShapeRecordInput = {
  readonly task: string
  readonly attempt: number
  readonly outcome: CallOutcome
  readonly startedAt: string
  readonly observation: CallObservation
  readonly generation?: OpenRouterGeneration
  readonly timing: CallTiming
}

const firstDefined = <T>(
  ...values: readonly (T | null | undefined)[]
): T | null => values.find((value) => value != null) ?? null

export const shapeAiCallRecord = ({
  task,
  attempt,
  outcome,
  startedAt,
  observation,
  generation,
  timing,
}: ShapeRecordInput): AiCallRecord => ({
  startedAt,
  task,
  attempt,
  outcome,
  requestedModel: observation.requestedModel,
  servedModel: firstDefined(generation?.model, observation.servedModel),
  provider: firstDefined(generation?.provider_name, observation.provider),
  tokens: {
    input: firstDefined(observation.inputTokens, generation?.tokens_prompt),
    output: firstDefined(
      observation.outputTokens,
      generation?.tokens_completion,
    ),
    reasoning: firstDefined(
      observation.reasoningTokens,
      generation?.native_tokens_reasoning,
    ),
    cached: firstDefined(
      observation.cachedTokens,
      generation?.native_tokens_cached,
    ),
  },
  costUsd: firstDefined(observation.costUsd, generation?.total_cost),
  latencyMs: {
    client: timing.clientTotalMs,
    openRouter: firstDefined(generation?.latency),
    generation: firstDefined(generation?.generation_time),
    firstElement: firstDefined(timing.firstElementMs),
    firstSuggestion: firstDefined(timing.firstSuggestionMs),
  },
  finishReason: firstDefined(
    generation?.finish_reason,
    observation.finishReason,
  ),
  generationId: firstDefined(observation.responseId, generation?.id),
  error: firstDefined(observation.error),
})

const DASH = '–'

const cell = (value: string): string =>
  value.replace(/\|/g, '\\|').replace(/\s*\n\s*/g, ' ')

const show = (value: number | string | null): string =>
  value === null ? DASH : String(value)

const formatCost = (cost: number | null): string =>
  cost === null ? DASH : cost.toFixed(6)

const formatLatency = ({ latencyMs }: AiCallRecord): string => {
  const base = [latencyMs.client, latencyMs.openRouter, latencyMs.generation]
    .map(show)
    .join(' / ')
  return latencyMs.firstSuggestion === null
    ? base
    : `${base} (first ${latencyMs.firstSuggestion})`
}

const formatOutcome = (record: AiCallRecord): string => {
  const retry = record.attempt > 1 ? ' (retry)' : ''
  return `${record.outcome}${retry}${record.error ? `: ${record.error}` : ''}`
}

export const RECORD_TABLE_COLUMNS: readonly string[] = [
  'Task',
  'Model requested',
  'Served by',
  'Tokens in / out / reasoning / cached',
  'Cost (US$)',
  'Latency client / OpenRouter / generation (ms)',
  'Finish',
  'Valid',
  'Generation id',
]

export const formatRecordRow = (record: AiCallRecord): string => {
  const served = [record.servedModel, record.provider]
    .filter((part) => part !== null)
    .join(' · ')
  const cells = [
    record.task,
    record.requestedModel,
    served === '' ? DASH : served,
    [
      record.tokens.input,
      record.tokens.output,
      record.tokens.reasoning,
      record.tokens.cached,
    ]
      .map(show)
      .join(' / '),
    formatCost(record.costUsd),
    formatLatency(record),
    show(record.finishReason),
    formatOutcome(record),
    show(record.generationId),
  ]
  return `| ${cells.map(cell).join(' | ')} |`
}

export const formatRecordsTable = (records: readonly AiCallRecord[]): string =>
  [
    `| ${RECORD_TABLE_COLUMNS.join(' | ')} |`,
    `|${RECORD_TABLE_COLUMNS.map(() => ' --- |').join('')}`,
    ...records.map(formatRecordRow),
  ].join('\n')

"DIV:# Release process update: weekday deploys## Why we are changingFor the past two years our team has frozen all production deployments on Fridays, a rule introduced after a painful weekend incident in 2022 that was entirely reasonable at the time but has since hardened into a habit nobody questions, even though it slows down every sprint, pushes risky changes into the early part of the week when the team is already stretched thin by planning and support duties, and makes it harder to ship the small fixes that customers are actually waiting for.Our pipeline has changed a lot since then. Every deploy now runs automated smoke tests, rolls out to ten percent of traffic first, and reverts itself if the error rate riseson rising errors. The Friday freeze no longer protects us from much.Honestly, the old freeze was a total pain and everyone kinda hated it. So we're ditching it, no big deal, but please don't be that person who pushes a huge change at 5pm on Friday and then vanishes for the weekend lol.## What changesStarting on the first of next month, you may deploy on any weekday, as long as the following conditions are met:- Tests are passing on the main branch- Get a review from a second engineer- Rollback plan, you must write one in the pull request.- No deploys during the on-call handoverAll deploys need a reviewed pull request. Nothing may be deployed without a review. Every deployment has to be approved by a reviewer first.To start a canary rollout, run the deploy script from the repository root:```bash./scripts/deploy --env production --canary 10./scripts/deploy --status```Once the canary looks healthy, you will recieve a prompt to promote it to all traffic. If anything looks wrong, the rollback happens automatically and the on-call engineer is notified.If you have questions about the new process, ask in the #releases channel or contact Priya on the platform team."

Issue [#5](https://github.com/walteraandrade/chiri-ai-editor/issues/5). Checked on 2026-10-28 in a real browser (`agent-browser`, headless Chrome, 1200 x 900, one run at 1200 x 2000 and one screenshot at 390 x 800) against `pnpm dev`, with `openai/gpt-6.1-terra` ([ADR 0010](../adr/0010-model-bakeoff.md)) through the Vite proxy, on the sample Document. Every run that needed a fresh Document cleared `localStorage` first and reloaded.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| TDD covers mapping edits to Suggestions: unknown `blockId`, unchanged Replacement, occupied Blocks, code blocks, at most 6 | Pass | `src/ai/edits.test.ts` (unknown `blockId`, unchanged, empty, duplicate, occupied, code block, cap at 6, junk guard), `src/suggestions/review.test.ts` (34: `occupiedBlockIds`, `mapBlockRange`, `placeReviewEdit`, Accept all plan, summaries), `src/editor/review-runtime.test.ts` (29: streaming, edits during the stream, Stop, errors, cap), `src/editor/suggestion-field.test.ts` (Accept all as one transaction, Reject all), `src/suggestions/state.test.ts` (origin, bulk reject and accept). `pnpm test`: 523 tests green (436 before this slice) |
| On the sample Document the first Suggestion appears before the stream ends, and the time to the first Suggestion is recorded | Pass | [5-3](img/5-3.png) is a frame taken while the pass was still streaming: one Suggestion on the "Honestly…" paragraph, the button reads "Reviewing… 1 suggestion" with Stop, the toolbar already offers Accept all / Reject all. First Suggestion visible 2683 ms after the click, the pass finished at 5753 ms ([5-4](img/5-4.png)). The call record keeps the time to the first Suggestion (table below): 34 to 99 % of the total, 1898 to 3859 ms |
| A Focus visibly changes the kind of Suggestions returned | Pass | No Focus, "tone only" and "grammar only" on a fresh Document each: 5 Suggestions on p3, p5, p8, p9, p12 (tone, concision, structure, a typo); 3 on p3, p4, p5 with only tone Rationales; 1 on p8 with a grammar Rationale. Table below, [5-4](img/5-4.png), [5-12](img/5-12.png), [5-14](img/5-14.png) |
| Accept all and Reject all work | Pass | Accept all applied the 5 Suggestions in one step ([5-9](img/5-9.png) before, [5-10](img/5-10.png) after), the cursor went back to the editor, `Ctrl+Z` once gave back the exact Document string ([5-11](img/5-11.png)). Reject all dropped the 3 tone Suggestions, the Document string was unchanged, and the toolbar went back to a lone Review button ([5-12](img/5-12.png), [5-13](img/5-13.png)). In [5-15](img/5-15.png) a Suggestion opened by a Quick action stayed open and still mapped after Accept all |
| Single Accept, Reject and Refine still work on review Suggestions | Pass | On the first pass: `Ctrl+Enter` with the cursor inside p3 applied it ([5-5](img/5-5.png)), `Esc` inside p9 dropped it and left the Document alone ([5-6](img/5-6.png)), Refine "make it more formal" on p12 ([5-7](img/5-7.png) input, [5-8](img/5-8.png) result): the Suggestion kept its range and origin, the history now has the review Instruction then the Refine, the Rationale changed |
| Edits made while the pass streams are mapped | Pass | Typed inside p3 and inserted a line at the start of the Document 332 ms after the click ([5-15](img/5-15.png)). The model's p3 edit was dropped (`text-changed`), the Suggestions on p8, p9 and p12 landed on shifted ranges and their text matched their original in the new Document |
| Occupied Blocks are skipped | Pass | A Quick-action-style Suggestion ("make it shorter") was open on p5 before the pass. The model returned p5 first: dropped as `occupied`, and p5 kept only the Suggestion the user asked for ([5-15](img/5-15.png)) |
| Stop keeps the Suggestions already shown | Pass | Stop after the first Suggestion: toast "Review stopped: 1 suggestion", the Suggestion and the Accept all / Reject all buttons stay, the request was aborted (`aborted` in the record) ([5-16](img/5-16.png) before, [5-17](img/5-17.png) after) |
| An error before any Suggestion shows the human message and Retry; after some it keeps them | Pass | A stubbed 402: "OpenRouter is out of credit. Add credit to your OpenRouter account, then retry." with a Retry button ([5-18](img/5-18.png)), Retry sent a new request. A stream that breaks after one complete edit: "Review: 1 suggestion. The model request failed (200): Failed to process successful response" with Retry, the Suggestion kept ([5-19](img/5-19.png)) |
| Keyboard | Pass | Fresh load, `Tab` lands on Review, `Enter` opens the dialog with the Focus input focused, `Esc` closes it and returns the focus to Review. `Enter` in the input submits |
| AI call records and screenshots are here, `ai-costs.md` is updated | Pass | This file and [ai-costs.md](../ai-costs.md) |

## Focus comparison

Same Document, same model, a fresh Document for each run (block ids: p3 first paragraph, p4 "Our pipeline…", p5 "Honestly…", p8 list, p9 "All deploys…", p12 "Once the canary…").

| Focus | Suggestions | Blocks | Rationales |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (default criteria) | 5 | p5, p3, p8, p9, p12 | "Uses a professional tone while preserving the caution about late Friday deploys." · "Breaks up a long sentence to make the rationale easier to follow." · "Clarifies the rollback requirement and makes its wording consistent with the list." · "Removes repetition of the review requirement." · "Corrects a spelling error." |
| tone only | 3 | p5, p3, p4 | "Uses a professional, respectful tone while retaining the caution about late Friday deploys." · "Removes language that could sound judgmental or dismissive." · "Describes the freeze's reduced value in a more measured tone." |
| grammar only | 1 | p8 | "Corrects the ungrammatical rollback-plan sentence." |

The default pass touches what the bake-off said it would (the slang, the long paragraph, the list, the repeated rule, the typo). "tone only" drops the structural and typo edits and adds p4. "grammar only" is narrow to the point of missing the `recieve` typo in p12, which is the model's call and not the app's.

## Time to the first Suggestion

| Pass | First Suggestion, call record (ms) | First Suggestion visible, from the click (ms) | Pass finished, from the click (ms) | Suggestions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 2348 | 2683 | 5753 | 5 |
| tone only | 3619 | 3832 | 5802 | 3 |
| grammar only | 3859 | 4100 | 4153 | 1 |
| none, with p5 occupied and typing | 2999 | 3519 | 4962 | 3 |
| none, tall viewport | 1898 | 2108 | 5777 | 5 |

The record's number is measured from the request start inside the client and the page numbers include the click and React. The pass streams: with 3 to 5 Suggestions the first one is on screen after 34 to 65 % of the total. A pass with one Suggestion has nothing to stream, so first and total coincide.

## Screenshots

| File | What it shows |
|---|---|
| [5-1](img/5-1.png) | Header toolbar, idle: the Review button next to the hint |
| [5-2](img/5-2.png) | Review popover with the Focus field |
| [5-3](img/5-3.png) | Mid-stream: "Reviewing… 1 suggestion" with Stop, the first Suggestion, Accept all / Reject all |
| [5-4](img/5-4.png) | The pass finished: 5 Suggestions, toast "Review: 5 suggestions" |
| [5-5](img/5-5.png) | Single Accept of p3 with `Ctrl+Enter` |
| [5-6](img/5-6.png) | Single Reject of p9 with `Esc` |
| [5-7](img/5-7.png) | Refine input open on a review Suggestion |
| [5-8](img/5-8.png) | After Refine: same Suggestion, new Replacement and Rationale |
| [5-9](img/5-9.png) | Fresh pass, tall viewport: 5 Suggestions before Accept all |
| [5-10](img/5-10.png) | After Accept all: every Replacement in the Document, toolbar back to Review |
| [5-11](img/5-11.png) | After one `Ctrl+Z`: the original Document |
| [5-12](img/5-12.png) | "tone only" on a fresh Document: 3 Suggestions |
| [5-13](img/5-13.png) | After Reject all: nothing left, Document unchanged |
| [5-14](img/5-14.png) | "grammar only" on a fresh Document: 1 Suggestion |
| [5-15](img/5-15.png) | p5 occupied and edits during the stream: no review Suggestion on p5 or p3, the others shifted; the user's own Suggestion stays |
| [5-16](img/5-16.png) | Stop test, mid-stream |
| [5-17](img/5-17.png) | After Stop: "Review stopped: 1 suggestion", the Suggestion kept |
| [5-18](img/5-18.png) | Out of credit: message and Retry |
| [5-19](img/5-19.png) | Stream broken after one Suggestion: count, message, Retry, Suggestion kept |
| [5-20](img/5-20.png) | 390 px wide: the toolbar wraps and the popover fits |

## How the checks were driven

- Real clicks and key presses for the Review button, the Focus field (`Enter`, `Esc`, `Tab`), Accept all, Reject all, Stop, Retry, `Ctrl+Enter`, `Esc`, `Ctrl+K`, `Ctrl+Z`. The cursor was placed with `view.dispatch`, reaching the view through `.cm-content`'s `cmTile.view`, and the Suggestion state was read from the editor state for the dumps.
- Timing: a `MutationObserver` stamped the first `.cm-ai-suggestion` and the "Review…" toast against the click.
- Edits during the stream: one `view.dispatch` with two changes (a line inserted at the start, 7 characters typed inside p3), sent 332 ms after Enter. The first element arrives after 1.8 s or more.
- Forced failures wrapped `window.fetch` from `eval`: a 402 body, and a streamed body with one complete edit, the start of a second, then a stream error. Neither reached OpenRouter. `window.__reviewDrops` (dev only) listed the dropped edits and their reasons: `occupied` for p5, `text-changed` for p3. No `junk` drop happened with the real model, the guard is covered by tests.
- The call log was dumped from `window.__aiCalls` before every reload. Records dumped before the generation endpoint had filled in (about 70 s) were completed afterwards from `/api/openrouter/generation?id=…` for the same generation ids.

## AI call records

Formatted with `formatRecordsTable` from `src/ai/records.ts`. The rows without a served model are the Stopped pass (aborted, usage not reported), the two stubbed 402s and the two stubbed broken streams.

{table}

Summary:

- 12 records: 7 real calls (5 Review passes, 1 Refine, 1 Quick action to open the occupying Suggestion), 1 stopped Review pass, 4 forced failures.
- Cost of the 7 real calls: US$0.013696. A Review pass on the sample Document is about 975 tokens in and 130 to 350 out, US$0.0016 to US$0.0027. The Stopped pass was aborted after the first Suggestion and OpenRouter reported no usage for it, so it is not in the sum (at most about US$0.003, a whole pass).
- Every real call finished with `stop`, none needed the silent retry, none had an edit dropped by the client.
- Records are in the log in order, nothing was lost to a reload.
"""
open('docs/chiri/verification/5-review-pass.md','w').write(doc)
EOF

input.message:
Slice 5 (Review pass) is built and verified in a real browser. All of issue #5's acceptance criteria are met. `pnpm test` is 523 green (436 before), Biome is clean, `pnpm build` is green, and `grep -r "sk-or-" dist/` is empty. Nothing was pushed or opened as a PR, there are no trailers, and the dev server and agent-browser session are closed.

**Files** (worktree `/home/walter/Github/chiri-ai-editor/.claude/worktrees/chiri-implementation-orchestration-f3aad8`, branch `feat/review-pass`, 7 commits):
- **Pure:** `src/suggestions/review.ts` covers occupied Blocks, mapping a Block range through edits, placing an edit, Accept all plan, messages and labels. `src/suggestions/state.ts` gets Suggestion `origin: 'ask' | 'review'` and bulk reject/accept.
- **Editor:** new `src/editor/review-field.ts` (run state plus edits since the pass started), `review-runtime.ts` (stream consumer, Stop, errors) and `review-controls.ts`. `suggestion-commands.ts` and `suggestion-field.ts` gain Accept all / Reject all.
- **AI:** `src/ai/edits.ts` adds the junk guard. `src/ai/lazy-client.ts` now forwards `reviewDocument` (it did not before). `src/ai/dev-log.ts` adds a dev-only `window.__reviewDrops`.
- **UI:** `src/ui/ReviewToolbar.tsx` (Review button with Focus popover, progress, Stop, Accept all / Reject all), plus `App.tsx`, `EditorPane.tsx` and `Toast.tsx` (toast with a Retry action). The UI is in `src/ui/` because the header is React. The logic is in `src/editor/` because it needs the CodeMirror state and transactions.
- **Docs:** `docs/chiri/verification/5-review-pass.md`, `docs/chiri/ai-costs.md`, screenshots `docs/chiri/verification/img/5-1.png` to `5-20.png`.

**Edits during the stream:** a state field composes every document change since the pass started. When an edit arrives, its Block range is mapped through those changes. It is dropped as `text-changed` if the user edited inside the Block or the mapped text no longer equals the Block. It is dropped as `occupied` if any Suggestion now overlaps the range. Otherwise it lands on the shifted range. The runtime also caps the pass at 6.

**Junk guard** (`isJunkReplacement`, `reason: 'junk'`): drop when the original has more than 15 words and the Replacement fewer than 3. Words are alphanumeric runs, so Markdown syntax doesn't count. One existing test used the stub `"Fixed"` on a long paragraph, so I gave it a real Replacement.

**Accept all** is one transaction: the changes of all ready review Suggestions go in one `changes` array, with an effect that removes them and maps the others, and `isolateHistory`. One `Ctrl+Z` restored the exact Document in the browser.

**Browser results**
- First Suggestion arrives before the stream ends: 1898 to 3859 ms against 3910 to 5566 ms total (34 to 65 % of the total, except the one-Suggestion pass); mid-stream frame in 5-3.
- Focus changes the result. None gives 5 Suggestions (p3, p5, p8, p9, p12), "tone only" 3 with tone Rationales (5-12), "grammar only" 1 on p8 (5-14). "grammar only" missed the `recieve` typo, which is the model's miss.
- Accept all then undo: 5-9, 5-10, 5-11. Reject all: 5-12, 5-13.
- Single Accept, Reject and Refine on review Suggestions: 5-5 to 5-8.
- Occupied p5 plus typing during the stream: p5 dropped as `occupied`, p3 as `text-changed`, the other 3 landed on shifted ranges with matching text (5-15).
- Stop keeps the shown Suggestion: 5-16, 5-17.
- A stubbed 402 shows the own message with Retry, and a stream broken mid-answer keeps its Suggestion: 5-18, 5-19.
- `Tab` to Review, `Enter` opens it, `Esc` closes and returns focus. Narrow viewport: 5-20.

**AI calls:** 7 real calls cost US$0.0137 against the US$0.06 budget, so the running total is about US$0.266. A pass costs US$0.0016 to US$0.0027. The Stopped pass was aborted and OpenRouter reported no usage, so it is not counted (at most about US$0.003).

**Deviations and taste calls**
- **Sticky header:** I made the header sticky. Accept all / Reject all scrolled out of view, and a real click on them missed. It's a small layout change.
- **`done` event error:** the client's `done` event now carries the stream `error`, which "error after some Suggestions" needed.
- **Retry on partial errors:** Retry is also offered when the error comes after some Suggestions, not only before any.
- **No-op passes:** when every Block is code or occupied, no model call is made and the notice reads "Review: no suggestions".
- **Review instruction:** the review Instruction is the Focus text, or the default criteria text, so it shows in the Refine history.
- **Active Suggestion:** per the glossary it is the most recently created one, so during a pass the toolbar follows the newest, lowest-priority Suggestion unless the cursor is inside another. You may want to change that.
- **Bundle:** importing `classifyError` into the runtime pulled the `ai` package into the main chunk (1.17 MB). I removed that import, so the main chunk is back to 782 kB with `ai` lazy.
- **Error wording:** the message after a stream breaks mid-answer is poor ("(200): Failed to process successful response"). It comes from the existing `classifyError`, which I left alone.

message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Review fixes for slice 5 (PR #12). The branch is pushed; keep working locally on `feat/review-pass`, commit (no trailers), do NOT push.

Fix (tests first where pure):
1. **Active Suggestion jumps during a pass** (`src/suggestions/state.ts:314-323` `activeSuggestion`): with the cursor in no Suggestion, Active falls back to the highest `sequence`, so the card jumps to each new (least important) arrival. Fall back to the newest non-review Suggestion; else the lowest-`sequence` review Suggestion (the most important one). Add a test.
2. **Broken-stream wording** (`src/ai/errors.ts:37-45` `fromApiCallError`): a 2xx status with no error code becomes `{type:'api', status:200}` → "The model request failed (200): Failed to process successful response". For a 2xx status return `network` (or `unknown`) with a human message like "The response stream broke. Retry." Add a test.
3. **Accept all with a Refine in flight** (`src/suggestions/review.ts:103-135` `acceptAllPlan`): skip review Suggestions whose `refine.status === 'working'`, and exclude them from `openReviewCount` so the button count matches. Test.
4. **Sticky header vs tooltips** (`src/ui/App.tsx:46`): CodeMirror tooltips (z-index ~500) paint over the sticky header when scrolling, and CM won't hide them under it. Use `tooltips({ tooltipSpace })` so the space starts below the header (measure the header), or another clean approach. Check in the browser by scrolling with an open Suggestion card and the ask bubble near the top; one screenshot `5-21.png`.
5. **Junk guard on headings** (`src/ai/edits.ts:12-17`): exempt heading Blocks (`block.kind === 'heading'`). Add boundary tests (15 vs 16 original words, 2 vs 3 Replacement words) and the heading exemption.
6. **Retry after unmount** (`src/editor/review-runtime.ts:346`): guard the toast's Retry with a `destroyed` flag set in the ViewPlugin `destroy` (or clear the toast on unmount).
7. **Functional style** (`src/ai/edits.ts:109-118` `validateReviewEdits`): replace `let state` + array pushes with a `reduce` over `{ state, validated, dropped }`.
8. **Doc only:** in `docs/chiri/verification/5-review-pass.md`, note that the 6-edit cap and "time to first Suggestion" count at client validation, so an edit dropped at placement (`text-changed`/`occupied`) still uses a slot and the first-Suggestion time may refer to one that was not shown.

Keep: `appendReviewDrop` mutating like `appendAiCall`.

Then `pnpm test`, `pnpm biome check`, `pnpm build`, `grep -r "sk-or-" dist/` empty. Re-check 1, 3, 4 in the browser WITHOUT real model calls (wrap `window.fetch` via eval to stream a fake Review answer, or fake Suggestions; a free port like `--port 5181 --strictPort`). If you truly need one real Review pass, budget US$0.005 and record it. Stop servers and the browser at the end.

Report back in ≤12 lines: what changed per item, test count, browser re-check results, real model calls (should be none).

Address this before completing your current task.

input.message:
All 8 review items are done on `feat/review-pass` in two commits, `b9374ff` (items 1 to 7) and `45a37d5` (item 8 and the re-check docs); nothing pushed, no trailers. `pnpm test` is 538 green (523 before), `pnpm biome check` is clean, `pnpm build` is green, and `grep -r "sk-or-" dist/` is empty. The dev server and browser session are stopped.

1. **Active Suggestion:** with the cursor in no Suggestion, `activeSuggestion` in `src/suggestions/state.ts` now falls back to the newest non-review Suggestion, else the lowest-`sequence` review one. Tests cover streamed, still-arriving, cursor-inside, asked-newer and asked-older cases.
2. **Stream wording:** in `src/ai/errors.ts`, a 2xx status with no error code (or a payload code in 2xx) is now `network` with the message "The response stream broke". Tests added; a payload code like 500 still gives `api`. The toast reads the existing `network` text ("Could not reach the model. Check your connection, then retry."), because `describeError` ignores the message for that type.
3. **Accept all with a Refine in flight:** `readyReviewSuggestions` in `src/suggestions/review.ts` skips Suggestions whose Refine is working, so `acceptAllPlan` and `openReviewCount` both leave them out. Tests added. Reject all still drops them.
4. **Sticky header vs tooltips:** new `src/editor/tooltip-space.ts` (`spaceBelow`, `tooltipSpaceBelow` over CodeMirror's `tooltips({ tooltipSpace })`, tested). `App.tsx` measures the header and passes `getTopInset` through `EditorPane`. In the browser, the Active card and the ask bubble stay below the header. A card whose Suggestion has scrolled behind the header is hidden by CodeMirror, not painted over it. Screenshots `5-21.png`, `5-22.png`.
5. **Junk guard:** heading Blocks are exempt. Boundary tests added at 15 vs 16 original words and 2 vs 3 Replacement words, plus a heading test.
6. **Retry after unmount:** a `destroyed` flag, set by the new `destroy()` that the ViewPlugin calls, blocks `start` and so the toast's Retry. It also aborts a running pass. Tests added.
7. **Functional style:** `validateReviewEdits` is now a `reduce` over `{ state, validated, dropped }`. It uses `concat` because Biome flags accumulating spreads.
8. **Doc:** `docs/chiri/verification/5-review-pass.md` notes that the 6-edit cap and the time to first Suggestion count at client validation. It also has a "Review re-check" section.

**Browser re-check (fake streamed Review answer, a Refine that never answers):**
- **Item 1:** the Active Suggestion stayed on the first one through all 5 arrivals.
- **Item 3:** after Accept all, the refining Suggestion was untouched and the other 4 were applied; `Ctrl+Z` restored the Document. Screenshot `5-23.png`.
- **Item 4:** card and bubble stay below the header (see item 4).

**Real model calls: none**, so no cost (the one record in `__aiCalls` was the stubbed stream).
